name: Almonds
notes:
Shelled almond kernels, nutrition from USDA. About 80% of the world's almonds come from California's Central Valley, so yield (~3 t/ha) is California data used for every region.

Almonds are famously thirsty: ~10,000–13,000 L per kg of kernels. That's a California orchard study (10,240) and Mekonnen & Hoekstra (13,080), most of it irrigation water in a drought-prone region. Emissions use Poore & Nemecek's tree-nut figure (~2.3 kg CO2e/kg).

Commercial almond orchards rely on trucked-in honeybee colonies for pollination (about two-thirds of all US managed hives each February), which stresses bees. That indirect harm isn't scored. Per-hectare pesticide (~8.5 kg/ha) and fertilizer notes were copied from the water note, so their exact derivation is unclear. Availability is FAOSTAT in-shell production × 35% kernel (FAO). Almond milk builds on this entry.
land_types_note: Irrigated Mediterranean-climate orchards, ~80% in California's Central Valley.

name: Cashews
notes:
Cashew kernels, nutrition from USDA. Grown mostly in West Africa, India and Vietnam, at a low yield (~0.7 t/ha, industry data), so cashews need a lot of land per kg.

Emissions (~3.5 kg CO2e/kg) are at the top of Poore & Nemecek's tree-nut range, because the shell contains a caustic oil and must be roasted and shelled by hand or machine before the kernel is edible. Water (9,280 L/kg), pesticide and fertilizer values have no documented derivation. Availability is FAOSTAT in-shell production × 25% kernel (FAO).
land_types_note: West African and Indian savanna, plus Vietnam's former tropical forest.

notes:
Pine nut kernels, nutrition from USDA. Mostly gathered from standing conifer forests (Korean pine, Siberian pine, pinyon), not farmland. It's tagged 'wild' for the Over-Gathering slider.

Emissions (~2 kg CO2e/kg) are the low end of Poore & Nemecek's tree-nut range. Availability (~35 kt kernels) is extrapolated from China's share of world output (International Nut Council). It swings with 3–5-year bumper crops.

name: Almond Milk (Unsweetened)
notes:
Unsweetened almond milk, nutrition from USDA (FDC Foundation Foods). It's only about 2.5% almonds, judging by its calories, protein and water. So land is the almond yield ÷ 2.5% ≈ 120,000 kg of almond milk per ha. That was corrected on 2026-09-26: the earlier Poore & Nemecek almond-milk land figure implied ~15% almonds and overstated land about 6×.

Water (368 L/kg) and emissions (0.70 kg CO2e/kg, cradle to retail) are Poore & Nemecek's own almond-milk values. The US water value is almonds' California water × 2.5%. Per-hectare pesticide and fertilizer are copied from almonds.

Almond orchards depend on trucked-in honeybee colonies; that indirect bee harm is described but not scored. Availability (~4.2 Mt) is a rough estimate from global market value ÷ an assumed retail price (confidence 1).

Vitamins C and K are taken as 0 from USDA's almonds record, since almond milk is mostly water and almonds have none.
land_types_note: Irrigated Mediterranean-climate orchards, ~80% in California's Central Valley.
sentient_harm_explanation: Commercial almond orchards depend on trucked-in honeybee colonies (roughly two-thirds of all US managed hives each February) for pollination; the resulting hive stress, pesticide exposure and elevated bee mortality are an indirect harm shared by every product made from these almonds, including this milk.
